SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) If I could give these negative five stars, I would. These are a four-pack of 64GB thumb drives that come in four colors. The first color, black, that I plugged into the PC hopelessly causes the PC to stall and become unresponsive to the point where I have to pull the power cord out to get the machine to turn off.

I tried the purple one after that, and it worked. Removed it okay. I tried the next one and hopelessly unresponsive again. That's two bad thumb drives in a four-pack. I didn't bother trying the last one as I don't particularly appreciate yanking the power out of my PC like that.

Maybe SamData is trying to sound like SanDisk? I don't know. I know that two out of four bad drives in a single package are statistically impossible unless you're just selling bad drives like an everyday business model.

Someone out to look into this as it seems a lot like fraud to me. These drives may well damage your computer since I had to pull the plug to get my machine back with two out of the four drives from a single package.
Worst thumb drives I have ever tried, bar none.
text_fidelity_b: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Tera Grand - Apple MFi Certified Lightning to Headphone Jack Audio Adapter, Durable Flexible Super Soft PVC Jacket iPhone 14/13/12/11 Pro Pro Max Plus Mini SE XS XR X 8/7/6, iPad Pro Air This is the first aftermarket dongle for lightening to 1/8" jack where the inline mic works as well as controls. I was amazed by this. What's much more impressive is that the fidelity of these DAC is outstanding and I experience much less distortion across the the full dynamic range on 15Ω dual-driver headphones from as low as 7 Hz. In fact, they performed flawlessly where other expensive amplifiers which no mic headphone controls (only the amps own buttons) worked at all. The Apple dongle doesn't really do a good job with larger headphone drivers which is why so many people get in line amps for their expensive earbuds. So
far, I’ve yet to try an in-line amp that’s worth what I paid for it. This guy is $20 and it does the job much better. I will never buy an Apple dongle or in-line "amplifier" again for an iPhone X series where there is no jack. This is clearly the way to go. Granted, there is no way to charge and have this control at the same time, but I guess this is a problem with the MFI spec from Apple. It's crappy, but no fault of this vendor. (It’d be great if Apple could be less thick about thinks like this and realize that people don’t always want to use a charge pad. It’s so silly.)

The design of this dongle is super rugged and I have not had any issues with distortion or phone problems. It seems just as reliable as the Apple dongle on an iPhone XS Max at minimum. I'm buying a couple more just to have them around since I hate not having my dongle nearby. (Tee-hee.) I’d just rather not have to pay the dongle tax to Apple anymore. They do wear out.

Also, I highly recommend the ERJIGO KZ ZS6 earbuds: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0756WVBZ9 as they pair incredibly with this dongle even at high volumes. I couldn’t believe that they sounded better on this than a fancy in-line amp! They sound as good or better than my UE Triple Fi 10's on the standard Apple dongle! For a total spend of $70 you are getting your money's worth and then some! Note, the fit of the Triple Fi is definitely superior to pretty much any earbud made, not to mention their noise-blocking capabilities. I doubt anyone will beat them there, but they are discontinued. (Thanks, Logitech.)
text_fidelity_b: Tera Grand - Apple MFi Certified Lightning to Headphone Jack Audio Adapter, Durable Flexible Super Soft PVC Jacket iPhone 14/13/12/11 Pro Pro Max Plus Mini SE XS XR X 8/7/6, iPad Pro Air

- one full charge lasts several days
- good way to track your BPM, Blood pressure, calories burn, steps taken

dislike:

Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa, 8" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th) We also have a 7 inch Kindle Fire (from 2015). This 8 inch Kindle (from 2017) is way better. It runs much faster and smoother and the screen is brighter and sharper. 1 inch size difference makes a big difference. This is a real bargain for $50. Added a $10 memory card to hold my media and this is all the tablet I need.

A couple of notes. 1) it is possible to install the Google Play app store on this tablet, but the user interface is very clunky. Many of the Google Play apps work much better than what comes with the Amazon appstore, though. 2) you can install some apps to your SD card instead of main memory, but they then load more slowly. I prefer keeping all my apps in memory and just storing data files (like audio and video) on the SD card.

Yes, all the Amazon ad-ware is obnoxious. It is spread over all the screens, not just the lockscreen. I am thinking about installing a 3rd-party Android launcher to remove most of it and give me a sleeker user interface.

Also, the speaker is really terrible. Very weak volume and poor sound quality; much worse than the sound quality of my Samsung phone. Plan on buying an external speaker or headphones for music or even for conference calls.

3.5 stars for user experience + 1.5 stars for cheap price = 5 stars

Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310 My experience with this extender has been good; it's significantly strengthened the signal in our living room, at the other end of the (admittedly not very big) house from our router. The one thing I've noticed is that nearby electrical devices, and especially ones with motors in them, will definitely throw this extender for a loop. We have an air purifier that lived first next to this extender, and then at a point about five feet from the extender, but between the extender and the router, and the extender did not like either of those situations at all. Lots of orange-light action (an orange light on this extender means no wifi signal). Moved the air purifier well away from the extender and out of the signal path and all was hunky-dory again.

I'm geeky sometimes and would like to be able to log onto the extender and muck with settings or at least make sure everything's good beyond what the green light tells me, but I don't seem to be able to do that once the extender's been set up; I can only get to the setup/configuration page after resetting the extender using the button on the back. But I'll live. The extender seems to be doing what we expect of it, and that's...all we expect of it (funny how that works).
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310

text_fidelity_a:
Guardline 500 Foot Range Wireless Driveway Alarm [4 Motion Detector Alarm Sensors & 1 Receiver] Weatherproof Outdoor Security Alert System for Home & Property Update Sep 2022, 5 years later:
One of the few things that has worked great through rain, sleet, snow, heat and all things Mother Nature can throw at it. Been very happy with this purchase! The sensor finally started having issues 5 years later and found the sensor screen cracked and condensation was getting in. Just bought another one! Highly recommend this product!

Update Sep 2018, 1 year later:
It is located out in the weather and everything has worked great through a year of use in our driveway; very cold winter and very hot summer. I changed batteries recently but did so out of precaution, not because the batteries were weak. We drive in and out at least 4-5 times a day, children ride bikes by it many times a week, along with several trips to the mailbox. About the only thing to watch is when replacing batteries the little screws will fall out if not careful so I placed a white towel underneath since our alarm is mounted on a post with pine straw underneath.
Excellent product and has been great, highly recommend. You can see my full review below.

REVIEW:
After researching several products including much cheaper alternatives, I ultimately decided on this particular brand/model. We use this specifically to alert us of cars coming into our driveway. If you are looking to use this for security reasons, be aware the sensor blinks red when motion is detected which can be seen at night.
Based on two week’s usage, I highly recommend this unit thus far and here is my pros, cons, & discoveries after a few weeks of usage:
Pros/Discoveries:
• Easy to setup and install. Read the manual first!
• Transmitter easily mounts to anything. We used a 4”x4” treated post mounted about 3’6” above the ground. Post is overkill but does look nice.
• Does not seem to have many false alarms but will pick up anything within the range of the sensor which has enough movement to trigger the sensor (as it should). Had one alarm over two weeks that we never saw the reason for the alarm. Perhaps something blew across the sensor. We also have a sprinkler system which sprays water across the sensor and it never alerts, which is good.
• Install the sensor at least 3-4’ above the ground which will avoid most dogs/cats/squirrels, etc., and do not place it on metal. I also would not place it near/within range of bushes/tree limbs or similar items which might move with the wind.
• Adjust the sensitivity distance on the sensor (you must remove the four screws on the sensor to do this). Our driveway is for one car so I decreased the sensitivity level to 23’ (set 39’ from the factory). Options are 13’, 23’, 26’ and 39’.
• You can easily adjust the angle of the sensor once installed.
• Has a sensor low battery indicator which flashes inside on the receiver.
• Easy to add other sensors if needed up to 16 (4 on each zone).
• Uses common batteries. Sensor takes four AA batteries (should last a year); receiver uses four AAA batteries and/or wall outlet power. Receiver can be plugged in with batteries installed acting as a battery backup if power is lost.
• Receiver has plenty of sound melodies to select (~30), and can be very loud if volume is adjusted all the way up.
• No problem with range as our sensor is only about 150’ from the receiver but does go through a couple walls.
• Our sensor is installed in the weather without any other coverings. Based on the instructions it can be mounted anywhere outside and I don’t see the need to put the sensor inside a protective covering.
• I like the removable top of the sensor to keep out weather and sunlight on the sensor.
• The 12 volt relay is a nice option for linking to alarms, gates, or whatever else you might want to do.
• Receiver is easily turned off and on. If leaving home really early on weekends for example, I’ll turn it off to avoid waking my family when I drive out.
• Came with a small screwdriver which fits perfectly to remove tiny screws in the sensor for battery installation and sensitivity setting.

CONS:
• I thought the sensor would have been enclosed in stronger PVC (aka thicker plastic). But it does have a lifetime warranty as long as the company is in business.
• Would have liked more color options for the sensor. For example, black, white and camo.
• Worried about losing the small screws when adjusting sensitivity and/or replacing the batteries in the sensor once installed. Our sensor is installed over a plant bed with pine straw, so I had to put down a white towel under the unit when opening the enclosure to make final sensitivity adjustments. Would have been nice if the sensor came with the type screws that don’t fall out when unscrewed.
• Receiver is not the nicest to look at but we managed to place it where it was centrally located in the house and not so obvious.
• There are over 30 melodies available but we were hoping for more chimes/bells similar to doorbell type options. Many are song type melodies which we didn't like.

Overall very pleased and highly recommend.
I would like to see a wifi enabled version for alerts on a smartphone if desired.
Will update this review should something change.
text_fidelity_b: Guardline 500 Foot Range Wireless Driveway Alarm [4 Motion Detector Alarm Sensors & 1 Receiver] Weatherproof Outdoor Security Alert System for Home & Property

text_fidelity_a:
Damero 2pcs/Set Portable Electronic Accessories Travel Organizer, Black I'll admit it right up front: I am an organizer junkie. I love having all of my things laid out perfectly and well organized in all of the different areas of my house. While I try to minimize as much as possible, if I do need to have a variety of items, and let's face it, electronics accessories and cords seem to multiply like rabbits, I want to keep them in an organized, attractive way so that I can always find what I'm looking for and so that they look nice on my shelves.

This two-piece set is meant to be a travel organizer kit for your electronics, but I'm using it in my office to keep all of the excess cords, cards, plugs, etc. for all of my various peripherals. It's fabulous, because I have one that I keep near my computer and one that I keep in my closet, depending on the frequency of use. If I need to get a cord out, it's right there, yet the cases are subtle enough that I don't feel like I'm looking at something overly functional all the time. It just looks neat, clean, and well-planned.

The quality on these is amazing. They are just stiff enough to hold their shape, yet flexible enough that if something's a little bit taller I can close the zipper over it and it's no big deal. The dividers attached by Velcro and so you can move them around so that it works perfectly around whatever it is you want to store and there. I've changed my mind a few times, and it takes two seconds to move the Velcro to hold everything perfectly in place so that it doesn't shift when you move the case around. I don't travel much, but if I did, I would definitely consider getting a second set for on the go. They are lightly padded and so would be a great way of keeping chargers, batteries, and other essential accessories safe. Honestly, I'm such a geek I would probably even use these for toiletries if traveling, because most toiletry cases seem like a messy jumble to me and I like how organized these are.

Overall, if you are on the fence about these, I would hesitate no longer. They are fabulous. I'm only bummed they don't make them big enough to house all the rest of the loose items around my office!
text_fidelity_b: Damero 2pcs/Set Portable Electronic Accessories Travel Organizer, Black

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS C100PA-DB02 10.1-inch Touch Chromebook Flip (1.8GHz, 4GB Memory, 16GB eMMC, Google OS), All Metal Body When my dog chewed up the cord to my 2012 Samsung Chromebook, instead of getting a new cord, I decided maybe it was time to get a new Chromebook. After reading all the "top five" reviews I could find, I decided to get this ASUS Chromebook Flip because of the excellent build quality compared to the others and the features. My partner has a Windows-based ASUS tablet this same size that he has really loved, so I knew the ASUS brand would be dependable. However, I didn't realize that this one would be the same size as his, but had I been thinking clearly I would have realized I would not be happy with the smaller keyboard size.

When the Flip came, I was definitely impressed with its build. Everything the reviewers said was true. I was thinking about sending it back, but then DP mentioned that he wished he had an ASUS like the Flip that could run Linux; apparently, he's going to sell his other ASUS because he's quitting Windows and the other ASUS machine has something proprietary about it that prevents him from being able to install Linux on it. text_fidelity_a:
Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker I have owned those annoying bluetooth ear pieces that always feel like they're about to fall off - or actually do. And although the sound varies from product to product, it's just not a system I am comfortable with.

This little speaker is simply perfect for my needs. It is 4 inches by 4 inches wide and only 1 inch thick. It has a switch that you slide to the right when you wish to enable the bluetooth, or to the left to turn it off. There is also another small button right beside the switch that you push in to receive or disconnect a call. A silver volume knob is sleekly incorporated in the overal design. The pairing was instant and consistant. No need to type in some code or wait forever for them to find each other. But here's the most important part - I hear my calls clearly and with no drop off or fade.

In all fairness, I only use this in my car and I don't spend ridiculous amounts of time on my phone when I'm driving. I've used other products with useless results. Half of the time I would risk a ticket by just ditching the ear piece and talking on my cell. In this case, I'm able to place it on the seat next to me and converse without any problems. Now that it's passed my tests, I'll be getting some velcro and mounting it to my dash board when I'm driving, and then just popping it in the glove compartment when I'm done.

The unit comes with a USB charger cable and it had a partial charge when I received it. Once it's fully charged and you turn it on, a blue light will blink for about 2 seconds and then go to a solid blue. According to the enclosed instructions, you will know that the battery is low when it blinks red. Couldn't be easier.

Musically speaking, my JBL and Sony are better designed for that purpose. But as a compact, speaker phone - this Phillips is without equal. Hands-free clarity without an annoying piece of plastic hanging over your ear. What more could you ask?
text_fidelity_b: Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) After initial euphoria, I have to say that the ROI is marginal at best. Briefly, here is why:

Positive:
1. Excellent day and night picture quality
2. Simple configuration and UI.
3. Free storage up to limit.
4. Rugged construction
5. Integration with Smarthings and other IoT.
6. Easy setup. Ensure you buy the condoms and mounting brackets for outside.

Negative: (Relative to price point)
1. Battery life is marginal. If you never have motion in an area great. But, think about that front yard where you have people walking by or cars parked just on the edge of your property. With roughly 10-15 activation per day, the battery drains quickly. I feel I would be better off with a perm. powered device.
2. While it has a standard micro usb port similar to virtually any android smart phone. You still require the Arlo plug to charge. Not a deal breaker, but painful.
2. App load times/camera viewing is slow. I have a 100 mb Xfinity internet connection with Netgear Orbi Mesh setup within 15 ft of the front camera. Connection in my house is not the issue. I have a Samsung S7 device. Be prepared to wait upwards of 30 seconds before authentication, app loads AND THEN the camera activates to see who is at the front door. It needs to be faster.
3. The absolute worst aspect of the camera is that recording does not start fast enough. Roughly 30 seconds of an event (or more) go by before capture begins. This is not acceptable. I have tried playing with various settings but unable to resolve.

Overall, I regret purchasing now. I should have invested the time and installed a fixed camera setup.

12-Jul-17 - I have lowered the stars on this product because of the incredibly poor support provided for both this product and in particular the ORBI which I also have. The warranty on both products which are similarly priced make zero sense. Stay away from NETGEAR until they get their act together.

17-Aug-17 - Finally heard back from NETGEAR and received confirmation in their user forums that the original screw adapter on the VMA1000 mount for the solar panel is too big. (gee thanks..I knew that) I was sent new screws that now allow the solar cable to be plugged in along with the VMA1000 mount. Why these are not highlighted everywhere and why there is no update to the Amazon listing as a bulletin or something to look for when buying the solar panel, I don't know. Overall, I would say NETGEAR is completely lost on any form of cohesive support and sincerely hope my product continues to work as I do not want to ever have to call or email again..

June 2020
I am done with Arlo. The product is over-priced and unreliable. Here is why:
I added the doorbells 2 yes ago and 2 of 2 have been rma'd.
2 of the cameras have been rma'd.
1 of the 2 solar panels has apparently died as not properly charging. This after less than 2 years.
I only realized recently that some Einstein at Arlo decided to have the wifi channel operate on the exact channel my mesh is on. There are clearly issues.
The camera has good and bad days from an access perspective. Some days they come up in about 30 seconds. Some they don't load..
The delay of 5 seconds before motion activates recording is brutal. You can completely someone moving fast.
Arlo support has become poor after being fantastic initially.

This product will be going the way of my Orbi soon. I am done with Netgear ( or formerly Netgear) products...

text_fidelity_a:
Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I'm having a serious problem with the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base that apparently the other reviewers are not having. I called Denon Technical Support and after spending a lot of time behind the TV set making sure all the wires were hooked up correctly and then pressing different buttons on the Denon Speaker base, they can't figure out what is causing this problem. And the problem is this: No sound signal is going to the Denon speaker base through the TV from the Roku player. The Roku works just fine through the regular TV speakers and is connected directly to the TV via HDMI. When the input on the TV is set to stream via the Roku no sound comes through the Denon and it turns off. If I increase the volume on the TV speakers you hear sound. If the input is changed to TV with the TV sound off, sound will come through the Denon. Also, if a DVD is played on the DVD player which is connected to the TV, the sound comes through the Denon. It just won't put out sound when the Roku input is being used. And that's a real bummer for me because we watch a lot of Netflix and Amazon streaming through our Roku. I am using the digital optical cord included with the Denon Speaker Base. I have it connected to the Digital Optical "Out" on the back of my Sharp 37" flat screen TV to the digital optical "In" on the back of the Denon Speaker Base.

I will keep working on this problem, and if anyone reading this has any idea that might fix it please say so in the comments section. I would love very much to have it work and to raise the star level to 5. When sound does come through the Denon it's great! Loud, clear and no buzzes or rattles whatsoever like when the volume is turned all the way up when using the TV speakers. I love that it can get loud and there's no rattles or weird vibrations. and the night mode is very useful since the TV room is located underneath the main bedroom and my husband has to go to bed early since he has to go to work early. I like to stay up late and watch Netflix/Amazon or other streaming channels through the Roku (oops! That doesn't work through the Denon) and I keep the volume down lest it wake him up. I was really looking forward to using the Denon night sound function.

The Denon tech suggested hooking everything up to another TV to see if the problem is the Roku player or my TV. Unfortunately, I don't have another TV to test out the units to try and isolate the lack of sound from the Roku player to the Denon. I was really wanting to use this for night listening, but since I can't I will take the Denon to my mom's nursing home and hook it up to her small, flat-screen TV. Since she's half deaf, it might can help her hear the sound better. I will update this review afterwards.
text_fidelity_b: Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding

Bose Portable Home Speaker with Alexa Voice Control Built-in Portable Home Speaker Charging Cradle, Black This is a great speaker! It has great Bose sound and gets loud!!!!
The speaker is very well packaged.
The cable has the same usbc plug in both sides. I will be buying the additional dock unit so I can just grab and go and not have to unplug it every time I want to take it somewhere.
The speaker requires the Bose Music app.
There isn’t much instructions that come with the actual speaker - it’s all online.
I already have the Bose Music app and was hoping I could just use all the settings I have already set up for another speaker - but it didn’t let me do that.
The actual setup process took me about 20 minutes.
The touch pad is very responsive and the voice pickup is great!
I don’t have to yell at it like some of my other devices!
The presets are available on the app and are pretty easy to setup. I set them up using both Amazon Music and Pandora.
In the Alexa app the Bose speaker is found under the Echo & Alexa group. It’s currently not able to be added to a speaker group as it’s treated more like a speaker than an Alexa. Hopefully an app update will change to allow this.
I also have a Bose Revolve (original) and Bose Home Speaker 300.
I am able to sync this speaker and the Home Speaker 300 through Apple Airplay 2 and the Bose Music app but this hasn’t been possible through the Alexa app.
This portable speaker has the same great sound as my Home 300 speaker. When they are playing next to each other they are in sync and make for great whole house sound.
Overall this is a great speaker with great sound and Alexa works perfectly! The setup was pretty minimal and it’s easy to use.
I like this speaker over my original Bose Revolve as I like the handle and I like to be able to tell Alexa to do things while I’m outside.
One issue I have is really with the app. I can’t seem to change the WiFi connection to the speaker without deleting the speaker from the Bose Music app.
I can change the name but not the WiFi.
I feel like I should be able to carry this speaker anywhere and connect to a friend’s WiFi or the WiFi of a guest house easily. The current way the software is set up, that’s not possible. I’m hoping there will be a software update in the future to fix this. Until then I’ll just have to use Bluetooth at those locations.
This was a little disappointing but nothing I can’t work around and doesn’t change the greatness of this speaker.

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions This GPS is a real upgrade for me, but I still love my old one which is TomTom One. Too bad it's no longer supported by TomTom or I probably would not have chosen the TomTom Via 1525 to try out for review. The very first thing I noticed about it was that the screen was twice as large as on my One - a very coveted perk to me. I choose to still use separate GPS devices instead of my phone since my phone uses up data and the GPS doesn't, saving me $$.

I have only used the Via 1525 a couple of times and it worked perfectly. I had to make a new account to TomTom to update it and overall it took about an hour and a half. I had a couple of problems with the update and had to restart but it finally worked. It comes with a USB for charging from a computer and another to use in the auxiliary power port in the car, and a mounting disk to adhere to a good spot in the car. It's not as intuitive as I would like, but it's not hard to figure out and it took us straight to our destination both times. I purposely passed some streets it was telling to me turn on to just to see how fast it would recalculate a route and it recalculated quickly. It has a lot of options that are indicated on the product page, most of which I will probably not use.

It's too early yet to give it 5 stars, but definitely 4 for now. It's a GPS, it found satellites quickly, got me a route planned out and was easy to follow. What more do I want from it? I like it a lot. It's supposed to have lifetime traffic and lifetime maps.......or until TomTom stops supporting it too.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

Orion 8923 20mm Expanse Telescope Eyepiece I have an Orion SkyQuest XT6 for over 10 years, and I've only had 3 eyepieces the whole time. Their standard Sirius Plossl 25mm, 17mm and 10mm. For the most part, the 10mm is pretty much useless, as the field of vision is so narrow that constant adjustments need to be made. I decided to give the Expanse series a try. This eyepiece is by far the best in the of the 4. Near Detroit, the light pollution is pretty bad. Viewing the plants and the moon is usually OK. My previous higher powered eyepieces usually made things look really bright and blurry. The Orion Nebula is usually a grey smudge. With the 9mm Expanse, I was able to see more shape to the cloud, and even a handful of stars in its heart. Cloud bands on Jupiter never looked better! I was also able to get a significant amount more detail on the moons surface than what I am used to. Looking at the sun was uneventful today -- only two sunspots.

Ultimately, this is definitely worth buying!
text_fidelity_b: Orion 8923 20mm Expanse Telescope Eyepiece

GAOMON PD2200 130% sRGB Full-Laminated Pen Display with 8192 Battery-Free Tilt-Support Stylus 8 Touch Buttons -21.5'' Graphics Drawing Tablet Monitor with Adjustable Stand I am a huge supporter of open source graphics software because I feel that the leading brand name software uses their virtual monopoly to bully people into overpriced, restrictive, nonsensical subscription programs. When I saw that this tablet was listed as being compatible with GIMP and most other graphics programs, I felt comfortable purchasing it for my uses.

However, upon installing it, I found that it is not actually compatible with the vast majority of graphic software except for those supported by Adobe, and a couple of other inferior programs. To clarify, it will still "function" with most programs, but only as a basic mouse. It will not support pressure sensitivity nor tilt. This, in my mind, means that it is NOT compatible, as pressure and tilt are essential functions for any illustrator. Without them, this is basically just a glorified mouse pad.

From Gaomon's troubleshooting website regarding lack of pressure sensitivity:

"The version of your drawing program might be too low to support pen pressure. Please upload it or try to draw in other drawing programs. Here do we suggest you some drawing programs. For windows system: Adobe Photoshop CC, Adobe Photoshop CC 2015, Adobe Photoshop CC 2017, Adobe Photoshop CC 2018, Adobe Photoshop cs5，Adobe Photoshop cs6, Adobe Animate CC2017 For Mac system: Adobe Photoshop CC, Adobe Photoshop CC 2015, Adobe Photoshop CC 2017, Adobe Photoshop cs5, Adobe Photoshop cs6, Adobe illustrator cs6, Adobe Flash Professional CC, Adobe Animate CC 2018 Other free drawing programs: Sai, Krita, FireAlpaca"

Contrast that with the information in the product listing, which says, "compatible with most of major drawing software such as Photoshop、SAI version 2、Illustrator、krita、firealpaca、gimp、SketchBook Pro、MediBang Paint Pro, etc."

GIMP and others are clearly listed, but are not actually compatible. This is highly misleading.

As for other aspects of the tablet, I can't say too much as I haven't used it very much due to this issue. However, from what I have found so far, the display looks good, and the set up is pretty straightforward, although their manual is extremely confusing to try to follow.

The buttons on the side of the display are completely smooth and can not be felt; there is nothing there to help you locate them by tactile means, so you will have to stop looking at your work and visually find them in order to use them. They are also located such that they are easily pressed accidentally when adjusting the position of your tablet, which gets annoying pretty quickly.

The chords that come with the tablet are a bit short, maybe 4 or 5 feet, which doesn't allow for much room to position your tablet if you use a PC that is located beneath your desk or to the side, especially if the hook-up ports are on the back of the PC. You can of course buy replacement chords.

The stylus is very lightweight, which I personally consider a positive but some people may prefer a heftier stylus.

There is not much lag when using the stylus; the movement is smooth enough for my needs. The pressure sensitivity, when tested in a diagnostic program, seems quite good as well. It just doesn't work with the software I hoped to use it with.

Overall the tablet is a nice size and has a nice display, but the other issues are factors you should consider when deciding between this tablet and a more expensive brand.
text_fidelity_b: GAOMON PD2200 130% sRGB Full-Laminated Pen Display with 8192 Battery-Free Tilt-Support Stylus 8 Touch Buttons -21.5'' Graphics Drawing Tablet Monitor with Adjustable Stand

text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

I have the RainbowLight color, which is exactly what it says: a rainbow light strip.

The rainbow light stays the same when turned on, the light doesn’t pulse or fade or change to any other color. The light can be turned on or off, there is no dimmer option. The rainbow light is visible when using your laptop.

The fan works well. It’s quiet and effective. The fan has a wheel to adjust the speed.

The cooling pad is height adjustable. The “legs” have two sections that fit into each other to adjust the height/angle of the cooling pad. The two sections don’t lock into place which makes me paranoid, they just fit into each other. It’s sturdy once you get the cooling pad set up, but I wouldn’t leave my laptop on it if I wasn’t there to catch it in case of something happening.

If using the cooling pad at an angle, the baffle is needed to keep your laptop from sliding off. The baffle is a small rectangle of plastic that stores in a designated spot under the cooling pad. There are no other safeguards built into the cooling pad to hold a laptop in place, so if you lose that piece of plastic, you’re screwed. I have other similar fans that have small ridges or foam pieces for extra security.

text_fidelity_a:
HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.
text_fidelity_b: HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA)

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam [[VIDEOID:bcc01f35bd32d1e66d3df81c3dace063]] Updated as promised: After working with the company I was able to completely secure the camera and still access it remotely. After all the initial problems and concerns I have had it installed and working for about a month I guess. It's working great on a variety of different software and protocols. I even tried connecting it to the Angelcam website and using DDNS. Works great with just about everything. With the 128GB SD card it does great. I uploaded some new photos of it working and the different clients being used securely. This turned out to be a great buy because the image quality is incredible and it's got an incredibly wide angle.

You cannot see the IR light like that at night it's only because of the camera I used you can see it. I did that for a reason so that everyone could see the amount of IR light it puts out. The infrared works great as you can see but the motion sensor even on the least sensitive setting picks up rains and bugs flying in front of it. Almost all motion sensors do. The audio sensor works great but the alarm feature doesn't because it's only one way audio. The email was easy to setup once you know which smtp server your ISP uses which WOW doesn't like giving theirs out even to paying customers. The video was provided by them and helped a lot because the screws were impossible to see and there are unnecessary ones in there that don't need to be removed. I have posted the material they sent me as well. I hope this helps everyone out.

BEFORE EDIT AND CUSTOMER SUPPORT:
So far I have had a lot of issues with this camera and still haven't got it to where I would trust letting it outside my isolated LAN which mean I cannot view remotely as of yet. I changed the 32Gb SD card out to a 128Gb card after contacting support since there is no instructions online or anywhere else on how to do it. Turns out it's the one tiny screw in on the top to remove the black piece and then you must carefully unscrew the lens cap. After that you will find several screws lowered besides the lens and IR area. You only need to remove the 4 of the screws. If you look really close with magnification you can see exactly what screws you need to remove because you can see how they hold the board underneath in place. Underneath the lens is the board that holds the SD-Card. Their support was nice enough to send me a video later on. I plan on posting that later after I get this all working. As of now it is telling me I need to reset the camera and there is no reset button that I can find. I am guessing it must be on that board again which means I am going to have to pull the whole thing apart again. In my opinion this is very poorly designed and not very good for people who like to customize or configure their devices. I do not like the way the it acts as soon as it connects to your network. I am still working on testing and hope I can get these issues resolved soon. The picture quality is great but there is a serious lack of security and other major issues plaguing this device. I am going to do some further testing and contact support once again about resetting this camera hopefully without having to dissemble it again but I don't see how. It has been disconnected for hours without power and will not reset that way. I also notice that the camera unit get's extremely hot for some reason. This will defiantly shorten it's life span. More to come on this product but for now I do not recommend buying this unless you are familiar with IP camera installation, network configuration, and have some electrical experience as far as handling circuit boards. This has been a real pain in the read since day one but I am hoping it will be worth it but time will tell. I will upload the video provided by them after getting their consent.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam

text_fidelity_a:
HP ENVY Desktop Computer, Intel Core i7-10700, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 512 GB SSD Storage, Windows 10 Pro (TE01-1254, 2020 Model) It is an alright system if you are only going to be doing basic computing like Microsoft Office, email, and some Netflix (but maybe not all at the same time). However, at a current price of over $850 being saddle with only the onboard graphics is hardly acceptable. Second, this system is also only okay if you never plan to repair the computer if there are issues with the power supply or motherboard. If you toss out your systems when they break, then this will work. If you like to swap out the bad parts, run for the hills you do not want to be stuck dealing with the HP part store.

If you want to play any games or use programs that require a bit more heavy lifting, (design software, CAD, or anything pulling a bunch of images or rendering) or need to have several programs running at once, you are going to struggle without a graphics card.

But can't you just add your own Graphics Card, I mean it is 2020 after all? Well... while this system does have an open slot on the motherboard for the addition of a graphics card it is severely handicapped in using it. For one, it is a very small case and you will be stuck with a small form factor card, which tend to be more expensive than their standard size counterparts. Worse yet, the included system power is only 180 watts. You cannot run much past whatever is already in the system with that, so you will need to also upgrade the power supply. Here is where it gets annoying. HP not only uses their own motherboard (Baker in this system) but the motherboard uses a proprietary connection to the power supply, so you HAVE TO BUY their power supply and only theirs. There is not an adapter, I looked and looked and looked some more.

That means heading over to the HP parts store website and trying not to pound your head into a wall with how backwards and outdated their system is. If you manage to locate the ONLY 400 watt power supply that works with the baker motherboard (yes 400 watt is the biggest they make that work for this case and motherboard) you will be hit with a $125 price tag (more like $150 after tax and shipping) for a power supply that should really cost half that. Which even if it says is in stock, will likely be back-ordered. They told me I'd be lucky to see it in 2 months even if it says "instock" in the system. Because they are the only ones selling it, you have to either wait or just forget about the upgrade. If you NEED it because your current power supply isn't working, well too bad for you.

If you have hung in this far and managed to get the power supply squared away, you can start on the graphics card piece. Now here is where it gets fun, you will want to avoid the HP parts store. They have the GTX 1660ti listed but its price bounces from over $1000 (yes a grand) to around $700 for a card that is about $300 on Amazon. Due to the power supply limitations a 1660ti is as high as you are going to be able to get, which puts you on par with an entry level gaming laptop. Due to size limitations of the HP Envy case you will want to stick to a small form factor card (generally that means one fan not two, but measure first some of those single fans are still a bit long).

So between the $150 power supply (that you may never get) and the ($300 graphics card off amazon) you are looking at about $450 in an upgrade to basically keep pace with a low level gaming laptop that costs less than what you paid for the HP Envy to begin with.

Which is my biggest problem with this system and the reason for the 3 stars, because it only does what it says (so earns its 3 stars) BUT if it has any sort of hardware issue down the line or doesn't meet your needs, you are going to be stuck buying a whole new system or be left to the mercy of HPs terribly unreliable part store with its over inflated prices and unreliable delivery timetables.
text_fidelity_b: HP ENVY Desktop Computer, Intel Core i7-10700, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 512 GB SSD Storage, Windows 10 Pro (TE01-1254, 2020 Model)

I’m also picky about mice, but am trying to be as ergonomic as possible in my peripheral choices, to prevent problems down the road. My current daily driver mouse is Logitech’s MX Master 3 and I use a palm grip.

I’ve wanted to try a vertical mouse since reading about them, but for me, the DELUX Vertical Mouse won’t be the one. The mouse is just too big for my small hand. To give an idea of my hand size, I wear a size small women’s glove.

My hand doesn’t fit naturally on the mouse. My whole hand slides down the body, so I have to keep tension in my hand and arm to keep my fingers in the proper place to be able to use the mouse buttons. It’s not comfortable; my hand and wrist hurt within minutes. My thumb keeps sliding to sit on the bottom of the side buttons, so it’s fortunate for me the side buttons don’t work on Macs.

I tried the mouse with and without the palm rest, there was no difference.

On the plus side, the mouse charges via USB-C, and can connect via Bluetooth or wireless. If you don’t use it, the wireless dongle fits neatly into the base of the mouse without impeding using it.

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

text_fidelity_a:
Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue These sound great. I don't have golden ears, but I believe I can at least partly tell the difference between good and bad headphones/earbud. I loved my last pair, sony buds that I only replaced because the cord finally gave in after probably 6 or 7 years.

The complaints about putting these in are founded, but honestly, if you spend a little time practising, it's not complicated and you can find easier ways. Sometimes I'll put the cord over the ear first, then fold the bud into the canal. Other time, the opposite. I tug on my lobe with the thumb and ring finger and use my index finger to apply pressure on the body of the plug to seat it in my canal.

I do run with these in. They block a lot of sound, but not everything. I' pretty hyper vigilant about my surrounding when I'm running, so I'm usually very aware anyway. I wear them to listen to music while working in the workshop and it turned the quite loud combination of my radial arm saw + shop vac into an EXTREMELY manageable background sound, and I could still hear my son yell at me to shut it off when he wanted to ride his bike in the garage - all without taking away too much from the music.

In less than perfect settings, like resting my head against a pillow (or car seat) they do start to hurt a bit after about an hour. General wear, however, hasn't really had that effect.

The cord doesn't tangle remotely as much as my previous pair, but I hope to keep up the habit of winding them and putting them in the pouch that comes with them.
I got the "black", but they are transparent black. I'd rather opaque, but really, it's not a big deal.
I do sometimes wish the distance between the "Y" where the L/R cords connect was a little longer, again, it's not bothered me enough to dock points, really.
I'd actually give a 4.5/5 but don't feel the need to take away an entire star.

(Update)
7 months it made it without a hitch. Then the right side started to flake on me. I have to contort the wire and get lucky to get sound, which usually stays fine until I remove them and have to do it again the nest time I use them. I'll be returning to Shure for a replacement, but I have to say that my previous Sony pair, with near daily use, lasted 6-7 YEARS without issue, so this bothers me. I'm certain Shure will replace at least the cable, otherwise I'd be dropping more than the one star I took off. I'll update if I have other issues with the replacement process or otherwise.
text_fidelity_b: Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue

text_fidelity_a:

And even then, parts of the data are missing. For example it may say I only walked a few feet a certain day, when I actually walked many miles. The vivoifit2 will have the correct amount, but it never sends the right data to the software any longer.

Actually really loved this item when I first got it. It worked great - accurately counting my steps. Wearing it made me push myself to walk further each day and also made me mindful of eating healthier. It used to sync fast and correctly.

I wore this kayaking - which I do several times a week and found it to be totally waterproof.

Sleep feature nice, but I don't really need that data.

The plastic band is a bit sweaty. I wore it super lose because of this. Even so, I bit uncomfortable to always have a perspiring wrist. I ordered the silver watch band, but after three weeks it still hadn't even shipped out. Glad it didn't since the Vivofit2 no longer works.

So in short, if it is OK that it only functions a few weeks, then this is wonderful item.But, if you plan to use for a longer period of time, this is not good.

Kindle Paperwhite – (previous generation - 2018 release) Waterproof with more than 2x the Storage – Ad-Supported When I was searching for a new e-reader after my first generation Nook lost its life, I began comparing the new Kindles to the new Nooks and I ultimately chose to go the Kindle route for appearance alone. At first I was torn between the more expensive Oasis and this Paperwhite, and I was also confused as to why there are so many Paperwhite versions available. I figured I’d compare the newest of both to make my final decision and although the Oasis has some light features I like, I chose this Paperwhite because the side bar (where you hold it and flip pages?) on the Oasis is just ugly to me. I don’t like that it’s only on one side making the whole thing off center. I primarily wanted a Kindle so I could get off of my phone more often to just read and I also needed something that provided a more natural experience for my eyes. My favorite feature of the Kindle is that I can put it on dark mode with the black background and white text. I even keep my iPhone at the lowest light setting with dark mode too to spare my eyes the brightness 24/7.

This Kindle is exactly what I’ve been looking for. It’s lightweight, slim, very easy to hold, and turning pages is a breeze. No clicking buttons, just a tap on the screen. I paired it with the leather amazon case in plum to match and it’s perfect. Sleek and beautiful. The light options are perfect for day and night reading, I can even see it perfectly with zero eye strain in a pitch black room. The screen looks remarkably like a real print book and it’s just so simple to use. I was initially concerned about the ads being too intrusive, but it turns out that they’re only on the lock screen and they just advertise books to read. I don’t mind them at all. My Kindle is only a week old so I can’t speak to much else yet, but I’ve been using it daily all week and the battery is at 97% right now without any recharge so that gives me hope for it lasting going forward. I’m very happy with so far and have found that because it doesn’t do anything like a tablet or phone would do, I’m reading more without such distractions. Leaving my phone down more too. Love it.

I shopped at a variety of stores. I was surprised to find that some of the companies known for sturdy cell phone cases did not offer the same quality to fit tablets. Notably absent was protection for the corners.
My search finally paid off as the ZUGU case is ideal. it is sturdy without excessive bulk. It protects all sides of the tablet including the corners. The cover projects a bit above both the camera lens and the tablet screen to protect them. The stand folds easily on the outside of the case. It is thin but stiff enough to hold the tablet at various angles and the magnetic attachment is a unique feature, securing the device without slippage. (I observed that some cases can flop unpredictably or are very limited in their options for viewing angles.)
Given the snug fit, I found it initially a challenge to attach the ZUGU case. . This is before I found the best approach was to slip the top right hand corner of the case last over the tablet frame. Due to the openings, the case material was s thinner and more flexible here. But do be careful not to pull too hard: The corner should slip readily over the frame here if the remaining sides are snug.
Another unique feature is that the company may offer to cover the copay if the owner has Apple Care and the screen breaks. (Please check the manufacturer website for detail).I
There is one trade.off with the case: it is purely functional rather than being a fashion statement. But I personally prefer protection to good looks and will enclose it with some confidence in a tote.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Arc Touch Mouse (Black) It couldn't be sexier. It couldn't be cooler. The packaging alone is pretty awesome, neat and spare and clean but with a certain wow factor. (It took me a while to figure out that, yes, there actually is a magnet in there that snaps the cover shut!) Compared to my Logitech V450 Nano, the Microsoft Arc Touch definitely wins in the design category. The handling is different, and it will take some getting used to, but I do like the look and feel over other Microsoft mice I have used in the past. The flick-scroll feature will be greatly appreciated by those who have to scroll through a lot of information. The page up/page down points might be handy as well but, again, will take some getting used to.

So those are the pros. The cons, for me, are more of a personal preference-thing. Some will find the click factor as satisfying as a straight-shift sports car. With my arthritis, I prefer the Nano, which is just easier for me to click. What some might find to be a certain yielding mushiness in the Nano, I far prefer to the Microsoft Arc Touch. That's just me. I also like that I have more control over how I define the behavior of my Nano over the Arc Touch; I'm actually quite addicted to my left-scroll "back" and right-scroll "next" designations. DH is going to love his sexy new mouse.

Finally, I had one weird thing happen when I went to the web site listed in the manual for a tutorial: The site looked nothing like anything from Microsoft and appeared to be a redirection of some kind. I didn't dare click on anything on that page. (If this is some partner of Microsoft's, then they should warn users in the documentation.)
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Arc Touch Mouse (Black)

I’ve spent right at a week with them and this is what I’ve found.

There are little to no instructions regarding these headphones and I had to research the app that has to be downloaded and go to the Razer website to begin using. Once I had everything set up, it was easy. I would have rather had a semblance of instruction than the wild packaging. The headphones were easy to pair to my phone and the sound is crystal clear. I was impressed with the noise cancelation especially. As an audiophile, I am very, very critical of sound and what is missing with these headphones is any kind of upper volume range or bass. For the price, I would have expected better in that department.

The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.

text_fidelity_a:
Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502 [[ASIN:B004QK7HI8 Paper Thin Leaf Indoor HDTV Antenna - Made in the USA!]]
The product works fairly well, but programs pixelate and freeze briefly quite frequently, as I have observed occurs also with satellite TV. If this does not bother you, it can be a reasonable solution for low-cost basic channels (mainstream networks like ABC, CBS, NBC, PBS, plus local access stations). Since I get most of my programming via the Internet, I could live without cable and could tolerate the glitchiness of over-the-air digital TV signals for watching the news and other non-cinematic programming. But pixelation bothers my wife, so it's a non-starter for us.

I don't know if any antenna, regardless of price or form factor, would eliminate the periodic pixelation of digital signals. This seems to be a problem inherent in over-the-air digital transmissions, but I am not a telecommunications engineer and may be wrong. There may be some antenna technology that defeats this problem. If so, you would have to compare its purchase, installation, and calibration costs to the payback period (months of no cable bill) to determine whether it would be a good deal for you. You can't beat a $0 monthly TV bill.
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502

We fiddled and fiddled and did what it said, after reconnecting the internet we had to clear the data. This fixed it , and it is now working perfectly again. My only complaint is that troubleshooting information was hard to find. Even the error messages were not easy to understand. In spite of that, if it had needed to be replaced, I would have been counting the days. I love this thing. It's sooooooooooooo wonderful to be able to watch movies and TV series without commercials. The picture is crystal clear and it's really easy to use. The voice search works extremely well. There are tons of free shows to watch, and free good music as well that you can play on your other devices free of charge. I will gladly renew my Prime subscription, even if I do have to pay for a movie once in a while. Also note, jaded Directv users- Amazon charges much less to watch a new movie. If I could get Fox News on it, I'd cancel Directv.  I am extremely happy with this purchase, even with the little problem.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold I've been wearing a smaller type fitness tracker for the past 6 months. Just started wearing this Misfit and there's a few things I don't like about it and many things I love about it.
I will start with all that I really enjoy about the Misfit. I like how easy it was to pair with my phone. Even though it sits higher than my other tracker, I like that it looks like an every day stylish watch and not like a fitness tracker. And it's very comfortable to wear. The buttons on the sides are more low keyed and not that obvious that it is a fitness tracker.
Love the sleep tracker of this smartwatch. My other tracker wasn't as good as tracking my sleep.
Step tracking is right on track with what I am walking. Very important to me.
I am still learning all the nice functions that come with this Misfit. So far I love the call notification and the alerts. Like that I can play and pause my music without taking my phone out of my pocket. I am still working on learning how to work my home smart devices using the Misfit but, I know in time, and with practice, I will figure it all out. It's not hard, I've just been really busy with working and haven't had the time with working with all the fun functions.
I also love that I don't have to take it off and protect it if I'm out hiking and get caught in a rain storm. I'm out almost every weekend walking in some nature trail or another. So I get caught in a few unexpected downpours while I'm out.
Now some of the more difficult "to do's" with the Misfit...
Setting the time isn't impossible, just need a lot of patience.
Using a magnifying glass, and good light, helped me get the misfit logo centered in that itty bitty hole at the 6 oclock mark. Whewww...
The watch doesn't have a backlight. So it's so hard to see the time in low light, impossible in the dark.
I wish it was thinner than it is. I'm not used to wearing a watch, or a fitness tracker, that is as thick as this one is.
I don't like the color of the watch band that came with the rose gold colored watch. All the other colored watches comes with a matching band. This watch comes with more silver colored band and silver buckle. Just doesn't look right. Might try to get that band replaced with something that looks better.
So far I am loving the Misfit. Love hearing that customer support is helpful in case I have a problem, like many has, with the crystal shattering.
text_fidelity_b: Misfit Phase Hybrid Wearables Smartwatch - Rose Gold

9/8/2020
Still enjoying this product combined with their oc200 and my pfsense NUC. The OC200 makes mgt of your WiFi a breeze. Stability is fantastic and speeds are still rock solid. text_fidelity_a:
Denon DSB-250BT Envaya Portable Bluetooth 8.25” Speaker (Black) - Lightweight, Waterproof & Dustproof | Up to 13 Hours of Battery Life | Hands-Free Phone Calling | Voice Compatibility with Siri This is a pricey Bluetooth speaker, but a high quality one so you do get what you pay for here. It’s one of my two favorite ones (the other is the Jam Heavy Metal) and outside of the Jam is far better sound quality than the several others I own. If you’re looking for something that gives you “adequate” music and can handle a splash or two, this is overkill. But if you want rich sound and insurance against big rain (or worse, a dunk in a pool), it’s probably worth moving up to this one.

Pros:
IP67, highly water-resistant. I confess, I didn’t test this by submerging it as it says you can; I’m gonna just trust ‘em on this one

Rich, distortion-free sound. Despite its size, this can get quite loud (in a nice touch for those wishing to pump it up, the volume controls on the speaker, unlike most I own, work independently of your source device (i.e. you can max out your iphone volume and then in addition max out the speaker). Even at high volume the sound doesn’t distort. And the bass is powerful and thick (not sub-woofer but then, if you want that, get a sub-woofer. For a portable speaker, it’s perhaps the best bass I’ve heard). It’s also quite clear. In comparison to the Jam, I’d say the bass on this is better but the Jam just edges out in terms of clarity with treble/voice. The sound quality is also quite good as a speaker phone.

Connecting. Pairing via Bluetooth was pretty instantaneous with my iPhone and iPad. There’s also an audio-jack to plug in

Stereo potential. You can link it with another, though I don’t have a second so can’t speak to how it sounds

Size: it’s small enough to toss easily into a backpack if not a pocket. Has a heft to it in terms of a quality, durable build-feel, but not so as to strain you carrying it around at all.

Cons are all pretty minor
Buttons are a bit stiff (maybe this will change)

No charging cable with mine

Neutral: no connectivity with voice activation like Alexa
Charges in a few hours and last anywhere from 8-12 depending on volume, not the best but far from the worst

Personally, I hate tinny, thin-sounding speakers. If I’m going to listen to music, I don’t need it to be pristine, but I do want it to sound like my music, so I think this is a good value. The sound quality alone is worth it—it blows away cheaper Bluetooth portables— and combined with the high-level water resistance, it’s makes it an even easier recommendation
text_fidelity_b: Denon DSB-250BT Envaya Portable Bluetooth 8.25” Speaker (Black) - Lightweight, Waterproof & Dustproof | Up to 13 Hours of Battery Life | Hands-Free Phone Calling | Voice Compatibility with Siri

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Before writing this review I glanced over some reviews of earlier models, and whatever issues previous editions of the Bose SoundTouch speakers may have had seem to have been worked out with this SoundTouch 10.

Setup was simple with the SoundTouch app (available for iOS, Android, and Kindle Fire devices). We had the speaker set up and operating in less than 5 minutes using an iPad. You'll need your home network security code to connect to WiFi and that's about it.

It comes with a remote, but most of the controlling is done from your device (tablet or phone). The remote is handy for adjusting the volume when you're using your device for other things.

The speaker is about the size of a cereal box. The sound that comes out is impressive for its size. I think there's a wee bit of case resonance in the mid range, but that's just me -- everyone else thinks it sounds terrific. It doesn't rival a huge stereo system but it's really, really good.

Now excuse me while I get on my soapbox about monaural. This is a single speaker system, not stereo, and that, to me, is a good thing. I'm a fan of monaural. It solves a lot of issues about speaker placement (trying to make sure they're equally distant), and you hear the full mix as the producers and artists intended. You can move anywhere around the room and not have half the mix disappear. And if you like oldies, particularly from the 1960s, this fixes the problems caused by common pan/mix practices from that era (for example, drums and bass panned hard left, guitars and backup singers panned hard right, lead vocals in the middle). If you listen to mixes like that in headphones, you pretty much have to mix the music down in your imagination since bass/drums are exclusively in one ear and keyboards in the other. Some devices don't support mono audio output (I'm looking at you, Windows phone), and as far as I know no one makes a dual-ear mono headset for phones either. So a mono speaker solves the issue. Okay, that's it for the soapbox. Back to the review.

The only tone control available in the Bose app is bass volume. But since the sound is well engineered, it's adequate. And bass is very audible. Not subwoofer level audible, but it's very present.

The SoundTouch app itself is impressive. It really does make setup a breeze. And the listening options are VAST. Hundreds of radio stations from around the world on WiFi, streaming music services, Pandora, Spotify, and so forth. I used to do a little shortwave listening, and if you're a DXer, this exceeds the capability of SW by far, and every station is digitally clear. And you can connect directly to play music straight from your device.

Just to be clear, the speaker itself needs a wall outlet to power it. It's not battery powered. But everything else is wireless. More speakers can be added, but it's so easily unplugged and moved around that one speaker can easily be sufficient.

Nice product from Bose.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue At first glance, the Razer Opus ANC Wireless Headphones don’t look like a Razer product. Where’s the green? Where’s the RGB? Even the branding is subdued.

These headphones are a grown-up Razer product, probably meant to be headphones you can take anywhere and not stick out as a gamer.

The Midnight Blue color is a nice change from black. I have a few pairs of wireless headphones and every single pair is black, so I appreciate having a little variety. Midnight Blue is a very deep blue -- so deep it’s almost black.

I’ve been trying the Opus headphones out for a few weeks and they have become the headphones I use every day. Before, I was using the Sony XB900N.

My favorite thing about the Opus headphones is how comfortable they are. The headband and ear cups have cushy padding. The headphones don’t squeeze my head too tight and don’t weigh a lot. I can wear these for 5+ hours at a time and not get a headache.

Sound quality is decent. I mostly use the Opus for listening to music and TV/movies. Compared to Razer’s gaming headsets, this isn’t one I’d pick for serious gaming. There is a tiny bit of lag and the low, deep sounds aren’t as punchy as with say, a Razer Kraken headset.

Razer’s claim of up to 25 hours of battery life seems pretty accurate. I didn’t keep a log every time I used the headphones, but I was able to use them for 4-5 hours a day for a good week before needing to charge. Unfortunately there is no battery indicator on the headphones to know when the battery is running low.

I don’t love the Razer Opus app needed to tweak a few of the settings. I have an older Android phone running Nougat, the app is incompatible with my phone. So I had to borrow my mom’s iPhone to install the app. By default, the headphones shut off after 5 minutes and I could only change this setting in the app. The app also allows you to switch between a few audio presets (but you can’t create your own) and check battery life.

If I take the headphones off my head, they automatically pause whatever I’m watching or listening to. I like this; my mom often talks to me when I’m wearing headphones, so it’s a lot quicker to just take them off and now I don’t have to manually pause. This is a setting that can be changed in the app.

The Active Noise Cancelling is what I expect for a pair of headphones in this price range. It’s decent. Not great, not horrible, but good enough to mute most background noise. But I don’t like that there’s not a light or indicator on the headphones to tell when I have ANC turned on.

The Opus doesn’t support Bluetooth multipoint.

The headphones charge via USB-C. The included case stores the headphones, charging cable, USB-C to USB A adapter, 3.5 mm audio cable, and airline adapter. The case actually has an outline on the bottom to tell you how to fit the headphones inside.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue

Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Another reviewer mentioned these issues, but I was impulsive and bought it anyways. They are all true.
- I spend a good deal of time adjusting the sensibility settings and using the brackets (both V and H) to reduce false positives, but they are still too many. My door is about 25-30' from the road and if a truck passes, even small cars, "motion detected". You stop giving importance for the sensor.
- I try to answer motion but it takes so long to load (I have an S8, with good wifi) and I got a connection problem way too often. If wasn't another false positive (as usually is), I would have missed the person lurking.
- The recording starts too late. when you go see the recorded video (because you were not able to answer the false positive motion), the video starts way too long after the movement started.
- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.
- I have installed with battery, that was really good because it was easy to install, but on the current pace (75% after 25 days) there is no way it will last the suggested 6 months on the website.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation

These ace those tests. Connectivity is not perfect but I am willing to accept that as it's bluetooth. I do get the occasional drop for no apparent reason but it is not often enough to be a huge negative.
They come packaged really nicely. So nicely you almost feel obligated to go slow and enjoy the experience.
You have to chose between the silicone or foam ear bud tips. The silicone feels softer and goes in and out easier. The foam will give you a more secure fit and sound isolation. I went with the foam and they do a fairly good job of keeping the outside world out. They are by no means 100 percent effective though.
I used the medium foam tips as well as the ear wings and find the comfort pretty good and the fit very secure. Wearing them for a couple hours was not an issue and I had no discomfort.
I cannot comment on their ability to transmit music as I use them for podcasts. Sound quality was fine for speech.
These have come down in price so much lately that I think they are a no brainer compared to the competition.
I dropped them a star due to the occasional random connection failure but overall I am very pleased with them.
