text_fidelity_a:
Fire Kids Edition Tablet, 7" Display, 8 GB, Blue Kid-Proof Case (Previous Generation - 5th) Very disappointed in Amazon. They ALMOST Got it right. Returned this one quickly.

Let me be clear I am an Amazon Fangirl. I have consistently tried their new things, I have subscribed to prime for years, I love amazon. I love their kindles. So I don't often speak ill of my precious amazon.

I wanted to upgrade my son's kindle ( First gen Fire HD7 ) it's charging port is a bit wobbly and damaged, we've used it for many years and it's got a little wear. That said, it works BETTER Than the current kindle fire. The only problem is you can't play all the same games that I can play on my other kindle and you can't on the new one either. It wants the "NEW HD" ( or my HDX) to play certain games.

Where to begin....first of all the new OS Sucks. It just does. so bad. I'm not even going to rant on that because it's user preference but I found the old OS to be more user friendly and responsive. I have an HDX and it's by far the top notch of them all. I hope I don't have to "upgrade" to this OS.

Storage & Offline use:
You only have 8gb of storage, which wouldn't be an issue thanks to the upgradable microsd slot.. ( GOOD CALL AMAZON) ..EXCEPT They crippled the functionality. For example, I go to the grocery store or road tip with my kid and I let him watch or play on his kindle without being on wifi, you can't do that anymore. Your kids can NOT Watch movies that are downloaded to the microsd card when you are offline. You can't. Not allowed. You can't operate much of anything in the kids profile if you are not connected to wifi. Having 128bg SD card is USELESS for your kids when offline.
I've bought loads of disney movies and the digital copies are all on Amazon for the very reason that they were great to download to our other kindles and watch when we were in the car, plane, or costco.

It won't even let you START The kids freetime profile if you are offline. This severely cripples the device for no good reason. Games and movies which are downloaded to the device or the SD card should work offline in most cases. I've done it on my HDX and my first gen hd. Works just fine in freetime on older devices. No reason for this. And before someone tells me that's what you expect when you stream...I'm not talking about streaming or using netflix, I'm talking about content downloaded to the device. Irrationally Amazon decided that if you are not online, you can go kick rocks.
If you are in an ADULT Profile, I think you can, although I did not try to be fair, because I bought the KIDS Edition for a reason, for my kid to use it.I have my own kindle. No sense in having this for kids if you can't use it when you're out and about. Everyone knows that the screen is the ultimate "quiet time" reward in our parent tool-kit. If you say it's not you're either a liar or an over taxed helicopter parent with way too much techno anxiety. Joking...sorry not sorry.

Kindle FreeTime "unlimited"....
I use the freetime for my son ALL THE TIME. It's amazing, it limits him to what *I* want him to play and watch. I can set a timer for weekends/weekdays that go off at bedtime so that he can "read", watch a show, or play for a short time as a reward before bed. The freetime is
the number one reason I have not gone with an iPad or other device. I can't give my kid any other device with the same level of comfort and control of his screen time and content. I HIGHLY recommend kindles to all my parent friends for this exact reason. It's WELL Worth it. However...it's NOT worth it to use "Unlimited" on this new device. The new kindle sucks for freetime ( See above reason on offline freetime) Mainly tho...it's TERRIBLE for the parent if you've mistakenly turned ON Kindle unlimited. ( If you have an older child, say 9yrs+ this can be mitigated with a nice sit down convo) I'll explain...

Why Freetime Unlimited SUCKS:
I'm speaking of the paid Unlimited service here, the main feature of freetime is still great, with some exceptions ( above) on the new device.

Every single app they touch it will download. If they are curious, and want to see what the game is they instinctively click the app, completely unaware that they have 8gb of space on their tablet and actually it's more like 4gb after the OS. This makes it run Slooooooow and crash. Crash a lot. Crash within the first 60 minutes of your child using the device. Until you go in and fix it, meaning delete them all individually, this device is annoyingly slow and unresponsive. I found out, you can get the apps to download or move them to the memory card, but it will still slow you down once that fills up and you still have to do regular maintaince on the devices memory. The first year of this is free, with this device, but I promise you it's more annoying than worth it. I was an early unlimited subscriber at $2.99 a month and I cancelled it rather quickly, even on my far better HDX and the first gen kindle it was STILL Annoying.

If you have an OLDER Child...this may be mitigated with a sit down conversation as to how their device works, what downloading means, and their storage space. My child is 5, and has proven to not exactly get the concept and download everything willy nilly if given the option.

Do yourself a favor....buy the HD Version, Pray they didn't cripple offline freetime on it, buy the extra warranty and case and and try that instead. That's what I plan to do, I'm going to give it a wait and see if they improve the HD device on the next round. Since the first gen HD 7 still works better than this one, I'll hold out.

Please Amazon....try to get it right next time.
Thanks,
Just another mom.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Kids Edition Tablet, 7" Display, 8 GB, Blue Kid-Proof Case (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) I really hate to use the word “cute” but there’s no way around it – this is a cute cam! It looks pretty much the same as the original Cube, but offers improved video and the addition of WiFi. Of the new features, the WiFi is the most significant, and makes this far more useful as a cam.

I also have the original Cube and the build quality continues to be very good. These are priced higher than the “no name” action cams, but after using (and breaking) a couple of those, it’s nice to be able to count on the Cube to keep on working. It’s water resistant, which makes it less worrisome when using it in bad weather or around water. It supports up to a 128MB SD card

The form factor and overall design is much the same as the original Cube. It has a magnet in the base that is more than strong enough to keep it well-planted. It’s not strong enough for significant activity (e.g., staying on a bike handle while riding) but it offers the benefit of tripod-like stability without the need for a tripod (providing you have something metal to fasten the magnet).

The biggest change is wifi on the Cube+. I found the setup to be straightforward – basically just download the app and follow the setup steps. I love that the app lets you use it as a live view – that’s a big improvement over the original Cube. It’s a very helpful feature for planning a shot, plus allows me to monitor how things are turning out without having to play the video.

Image quality has been impressive – zero complaints there. I was pleased with the resolution of the original Cube, and this is a bit better. Audio quality is OK. It’s not outstanding, but it clearly picks up voices. I understand that earlier versions of the Cube+ had very poor sound quality, but the one I have (got it in Dec 2015) is fine with regard to sound.

All in all, it’s a great cam with a fun form factor and look. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a small profile action cam with solid build quality and performance. While the price has increased over that of the original Cube, the wifi features are very useful and well implemented, making this version well worth the additional cost.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Update: I have now tried two other brands (a coworker's, and bought another brand) of ergonomic mice that both work substantially better than the Anker version, which also cost less! I highly suggest anyone considering buying this, skip over it and look for another one that is cheaper with good reviews. It amazes me that a company with a known name can skip out on quality so much that other product that cost half as much outperform it in every way.

The Good:
Feels great to hold. More natural than a typical mouse. All the buttons are in the right places and do not require any strain to press. The wheel is in the perfect spot to be used by my middle finger, which is typically what I try to do, since I swear I already have arthritis in my point finger being under 30 years old...

The Bad: There is an obvious input delay, making this pretty terrible for anyone who grew up using computers. That no one else has mentioned this is beyond me. Side by side comparison of any of my Logitech mice and this Anker mouse makes the input delay on this mouse even more obvious. It feels like trying to use a mouse on a TV with interpolation (120 Hz, smooth motion, etc.) enabled. On top of the nearly deal-breaking latency issue, the input into the computer is inconsistent, causing the mouse to frequently skip around or miss my movements.

If you expect to play any game that requires any amount of precision or is time-based, you will regret buying this mouse. Games aside, this mouse reduces my productivity because of how unreliable the signal is, and the extra effort needed to predict the movement of the cursor due to the lag.

I tried the wired version of this mouse (a friend had it) and the input lag is not as bad, but is still there. Therefore, I advise against anyone buying this or the wired version, and suggest to instead look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer Okay. At first I was not impressed with the Harmony Ultimate. After getting the system up and going, however, I love it.

Desired goal: control two entertainment systems in two rooms with four remotes -- two in each room.

3/29/16 update: I thought having a single remote talking to a single hub was a drawback. But the app on my iPhone is so effective, it's really a second remote for no extra cost. I don't even touch the actual remote that came with the system. That's for the wife, who has taken to the system easily and understands how to work it. I now love my system. Five stars.

3/17/16 Logitech Ultimate Remote w/Hub
Cons:
1. Only one remote can be paired with each hub. Want the wife to have her own remote on one side of the room and you to have another, both controlling the same equipment? Forget it. You can't.
2. Two hubs cannot talk to each other. So you buy two remotes and two hubs, thinking they will talk to each other over WiFi? Forget it. They can't.
3. Pricey at list. Acceptable when on sale ($120 off is nice)

Pros:
1. Excellent phone app. You do all programming from the phone after you create a Logitech cloud account. This gives you control of your system if your phone can reach the internet.
2. Excellent desktop app. Logitech has given up trying to use browsers; you use genuine local apps on your phone and laptop.
3. Easy to set up: Enter MFG and Model number for each device. Done. Full remote buttons download for each device.
4. Touch screen on both the remote and the app has "gestures" with one- or two-finger swiping to control devices. This is nice and unexpected.
5. Colorful
6. Recharges in the cradle -- no more AAA batteries!
7. Wakes up when you pick it up
8. Backlit buttons
9. Haptic feedback when a virtual button is pressed
10. Phone app is great for setup and works as a second remote.

Setting up the first remote was wonderful and very exciting. I couldn't wait to expand the system with my second hub and its remote to create a really capable, flexible system. When the second hub failed to talk to the first hub and I discovered that I had purchased two systems that cannot talk to each other, my elation went to mild disappointment.

Sequence to set up:

1. Create an account with Logitech Harmony at myharmony.com
2. Download the Harmony phone app and download the desktop exe to your laptop.
3. Log in to the account
4. Name and connect the first hub with you WiFi router password
5. Add devices to the room's hub by entering the Manufacturer and the Model number for each device
a. These devices can be far more than AV devices, including lights, blinds, thermostats and other things to a limit of 15.
b. Each device can be renamed for accurate familiarity
6. Create "Activities" for the devices you want to control:
I.e., "Blu-ray Living Rm"
a. it will ask first, "what devices are involved in this activity?"
b. checkbox "AV receiver Living Rm," "TV Living Rm," and "Blu-ray Living Rm"
c. the app asks, "Which input for the TV?" and "Which input for the AV Receiver?" and "Which device controls the volume?"
d. click "run test" to see if everything shuts off and turns back on correctly
e. if it's good, click "yes." Good to go to create next activity.

After you get one room's devices entered and working, if you have a second hub and remote, program it separately in the next room. You can rename the hubs using the desktop exe, but not from the phone app. This is very helpful if you are using the phone as a second remote. You'll have to switch hubs on the phone if you go from one room to another.

You can reorder the activities on both the phone and the remote for most logical order for that room
You can edit buttons and gestures and more.
You can add delay time if a unit needs more time to warm up before it can receive a command
You can change the timeout for the remote to go into standby
You can use your phone as a fully functional remote, but you do have to select which hub you want to talk to.
The Hub connects wirelessly to your WiFi router. It also acts as a giant IR blaster to send commands to the devices. It also has two 2.5mm mono sub-mini plug sockets and two "mini blaster" IR emitters that plug into these sockets so you can send IR to other places.

If you have a device in another room that needs to be controlled, you can extend one of the mini-blasters using an inexpensive 2.5mm extension cord like the 5-meter [[ASIN:B003OSR5TE kenable 2.5mm Stereo Jack Plug to 2.5mm Jack Socket Extension Cable 5m (~16.5 feet)]] or a wireless remote IR extension system like the [[ASIN:B0087S9CJ2 Monoprice 109194 Wireless Dual Band IR Remote Control Extender Upto 328-Feet]].

This wired or wireless extension to another room would be moot if the hubs talked to each other.

What Logitech needs to make happen is to allow multiple remotes to talk to multiple hubs and for the hubs to talk to each other. They've been promising this added capability since at least 2013 on their forums, but so far, it's one remote to one hub and workarounds.

Logitech should not market this as "Ultimate." It's very capable, but also not quite as flexible as required.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Ultimate All in One Remote - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
Beats Flex Wireless Earbuds – Apple W1 Headphone Chip, Magnetic Earphones, Class 1 Bluetooth, 12 Hours of Listening Time, Built-in Microphone - Yuzu Yellow Pros: great sound, and has amazing battery life. Little magnets click to hold the earbuds together around your neck if you aren't using them, and the audio stream automatically turns off in this position. And, the stream turns on again when separated, if the earbuds are still on. Pairs easily with other devices, unlike other earbuds that I've tried, which seem to get very confused and would only turn one ear on, or was finicky and didn't want to connect, etc. These connect quickly and surely (I don't know how else to put it!).

Cons: none really. The only (mild) complaint I have is that the light that indicates whether or not the earbuds are still on after they've been hanging around your neck without being used is in a spot that's hard to see. You kind of have to skootch the whole thing away from yourself so it's not directly under your chin where you can't see it, and even then, you have to angle the switch toward you to see whether the light is on. (Such First World Problems.) Beyond that, no other complaints!
text_fidelity_b: Beats Flex Wireless Earbuds – Apple W1 Headphone Chip, Magnetic Earphones, Class 1 Bluetooth, 12 Hours of Listening Time, Built-in Microphone - Yuzu Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.
text_fidelity_b: Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function.
